original_question: Is it consistent that the continuum c is strictly larger than ℵ2 and that for every cardinal κ in the interval [ℵ1, c], every 2-coloring of κ×ω has a monochromatic rectangle of sizes κ and ω, i.e. \( inom{\kappa}{\omega} 	o  inom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\)?
target_in_paper: Problem 3.13 in Section 3, “Polarized partition relations at the first infinite cardinal.” ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem almost verbatim: it asks whether one can have 𝔠 > ℵ₂ and simultaneously have the strong polarized relation (κ over ω) → (κ over ω)^{1,1}_2 for every cardinal κ in the full interval [ℵ₁, 𝔠]. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
missing_details: State explicitly that the question is about consistency with ZFC.
Use the standard notation 𝔠 = 2^{ℵ₀} rather than plain c, so the question is fully stand-alone.
Make explicit that the interval [ℵ₁, 𝔠] is inclusive and ranges over cardinals κ.
Spell out the partition relation in functional form: for every coloring c: κ × ω → 2 there exist A ⊆ κ and B ⊆ ω with |A| = κ and |B| = ω such that c restricted to A × B is constant.
Do not add the stronger extra hypothesis 𝔰 = 𝔠; that belongs to the neighboring Problem 3.14, not to the target Problem 3.13. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
refined_question: Is it consistent with ZFC that 𝔠 = 2^{ℵ₀} is strictly larger than ℵ₂ and that, for every cardinal κ with ℵ₁ ≤ κ ≤ 𝔠, every coloring c: κ × ω → 2 admits sets A ⊆ κ and B ⊆ ω such that |A| = κ, |B| = ω, and c restricted to A × B is constant; equivalently, that (κ over ω) → (κ over ω)^{1,1}_2 for every κ ∈ [ℵ₁, 𝔠]?
justification: The paper first notes that the spectrum statement “for every κ ∈ [ℵ₁, 𝔠], (κ over ω) → (κ over ω)^{1,1}_2” is consistent in a model with 𝔠 = ℵ₂, and then immediately asks whether the same can hold with 𝔠 > ℵ₂; this is exactly Problem 3.13. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf)) Your draft therefore targets Problem 3.13 rather than the stronger neighboring Problem 3.14, which additionally assumes 𝔰 = 𝔠 > ℵ₂. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf)) The meaning of the strong polarized relation itself is given earlier in Definition 1.1: for every coloring c: λ × κ → 2 there are A ⊆ λ and B ⊆ κ with |A| = λ and |B| = κ such that c on A × B is constant. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
